value: :1:\d+: error: non-integral type '(uint3|vector<uint, ?3>)' is an invalid underlying type
note: Ask 2 of #4384 -- diagnostic quality. *** POLARITY IS INVERTED relative to match.json. *** A MATCH here means the compiler DID say the right thing, i.e. this half of the issue is SATISFIED on that build; a no-match means it did not, i.e. the symptom the title asks about ('rather than error') is present. Read a bisect over this file as the history of the *fix*, not of the bug. The inversion is deliberate: the symptom is an absence, and an absence predicate is satisfied for free by any build that rejects the command line, the language version or the profile before ever parsing the enum -- that trap manufactures a reproduction on exactly the oldest releases. A presence predicate is self-anchoring, so it cannot. Anchored on ':1:<col>:' because the enum-base is line 1 of every source in this directory, which proves the diagnostic is about this construct and not something else; the type spelling is pinned to the vector so that a well-formed message about a different subject cannot satisfy it. Controls: control-uint3-scalar-init.hlsl (same invalid underlying type, scalar enumerator) must MATCH -- it proves the predicate can fire and that this exact wording exists for this exact type; control-valid-enum.hlsl and control-float-enum.hlsl must NOT match.
